This is the first release of Origins. Origins is genealogy software that stores a
family tree as text files in a git repository. Each person, family, place, source and
hypothesis is a Markdown file with YAML frontmatter.

To install it, follow [Install](https://origins-project.github.io/origins/install) on
the site. [Getting started](https://origins-project.github.io/origins/getting-started)
shows you how to make a first corpus. You can try the pages without installing anything
in the [demo](https://origins-project.github.io/origins/demo/index.html).

This release has:

- The corpus format. People, families, places, sources, repositories, notes and
  hypotheses are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter, one directory for each record.
- `origins init` to start a corpus, `check` to look for contradictions in it, `fmt` to
  rewrite it in canonical form, and `todo` to list the research still to do.
- The commands that change a corpus: `set`, `unset`, `add`, `remove`, `create`,
  `rename`, `delete`, `merge` and `split`. Origins records each change as a git
  commit. You can read that history with `log`, `whence`, `blame` and `why`, and take
  back the last change with `undo`.
- `origins adopt` to record changes you made to the files with an editor.
- Hypotheses. You can test one with `check --with`, and settle it with
  `hypothesis accept` or `hypothesis reject`.
- Import from GEDCOM and from Gramps, with `origins import gedcom` and
  `origins import gramps`.
- Export to GEDCOM 7.0, to charts in SVG, PDF and PNG, and to a folder of web pages,
  with `origins export`.
- `origins browse`, which shows the corpus in a browser, where you can also change it.
- `origins mcp`, which serves the corpus to an AI agent over the Model Context
  Protocol. The agent can read the corpus and propose hypotheses.
- Sharing a corpus through git remotes with `remote`, `fetch`, `push`, `pull` and
  `clone`.
- Archives for Linux, macOS and Windows on amd64 and arm64, and a Docker image for
  linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 at `ghcr.io/origins-project/origins`.
